headline_stat.name: fraction of decodable SWR events with significant sequential structure (p<0.05 vs 500x time-bin shuffle)

stated_limitation: an unrestricted, whole-recording baseline turned out to be dominated by movement-related broadband artifacts (high ripple-band power samples were *less* likely to be immobile than chance), so gating on immobility first was necessary to get physiologically plausible events

justification.dataset: DANDI 000447 CA1 W-track (Frank/Jadhav) is the canonical hippocampal replay preparation, an expert-standard choice.
justification.handling: Real streamed data with correct unit/LFP/position/epoch alignment, explicit place-cell criteria, and immobility-gated ripple detection backed by an empirical artifact check.
justification.analysis: Bayesian decoding with a per-event time-bin shuffle null is a standard, correctly implemented replay analysis, though no formal population test is run and the score/significance decoupling is unaddressed.
justification.correctness: The 7/23 (30%) headline reproduces exactly from the committed CSV and is internally consistent and physically possible.
justification.figures: Population and place-field figures are strong, but the local/remote example events are selected by distance-from-position rather than replay strength, so the 'remote' figure shows an incoherent score-0.05 posterior, capping this axis.
justification.honesty: The population claim is honest and transparent, but the prose presents the visibly diffuse, near-zero-score remote example as a coherent trajectory sweep with no caveat, misrepresenting an unrepresentative exemplar.
justification.verdict: The core population-level replay demonstration is sound and reproduces, so the science warrants revision rather than rejection, but the remote-example misrepresentation fails the honesty gate.
